param.name: in_features
param.dialogReference: Features to evaluate for proximity. For REST requests, provide a layer object with a url property, for example {"url": "https://.../FeatureServer/0"}.

param.name: input_where_clause
param.dialogReference: Optional SQL expression used to filter input features before proximity analysis. Use a physical field name from the input layer schema, not a field alias, and a verified value. For example, DAMAGE_CLASS = 'High Damage Evidence' only when DAMAGE_CLASS and that value exist in the selected layer. Leave blank to evaluate all input features.

param.name: proximity_features
param.dialogReference: Reference features used to find nearby input features. For REST requests, provide a layer object with a url property, for example {"url": "https://.../FeatureServer/0"}.

param.name: proximity_where_clause
param.dialogReference: Optional SQL expression used to filter proximity features before analysis. Use a physical field name from the proximity layer schema, not a field alias, and a verified value. For example, DAMAGE_CLASS = 'High Damage Evidence' only when DAMAGE_CLASS and that value exist in the selected layer. Leave blank to use all proximity features.

param.name: search_distance
param.dialogReference: Geodesic distance used for the selection. Example: 500 Meters or 2 Miles.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: New feature class containing input features within the search distance. Example: C:\data\analysis.gdb\issues_near_schools.

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Returns input features within a user-specified geodesic distance of user-supplied reference features.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Use this tool when the features to evaluate and the reference features must be chosen at run time. Before supplying either optional SQL where clause, inspect the selected layer's schema and use its physical field names and verified values, not display aliases. The SQL must use the dialect accepted by the referenced feature service. For example, use DAMAGE_CLASS = 'High Damage Evidence' only when DAMAGE_CLASS and that value are confirmed in the selected layer. Leave a where clause blank to include all features from that layer.
